name: shingle
summary: A shake roof: split wooden tiles laid in overlapping courses, mossed on the north side.
why: Not timber, and the difference is the whole point of a separate file. timber is a sawn
board lying flat - a fence rail, a lamp post - with grain running along it and 0.22 of
depth. A roof is a hundred small boards each standing a centimetre proud of the one below,
so what the eye reads is the step between courses rather than the grain on any of them.
Depth 0.40, second only to cobble's 0.45 and for exactly the same reason: the shadow line
under each course is real, it is drawn as near-black in the art, and it is the whole of why
a roof reads as a roof rather than as a green rectangle.
Roughness 0.90. Split wood that has been rained on for twenty years and has moss in its
gaps. There is no angle at which a shake roof has a highlight.
Cast rather than brushed, which is the one surprise here. The boards do have a grain and it
does run one way, but at a roof's distance the grain is invisible and the courses are not -
and a brushed normal would run its scratches along the roof rather than across it, which is
the opposite of the direction that matters.
